title: Swift UV data limit the UV yield of one late-debris model for ASASSN-14ko
abstract: A published debris model preserves the ASASSN-14ko event clock through a shared return delay and conserves orbital energy and angular momentum with a later gas component. We test the UV output of its finite equal-mass reference band. After aligning the first primary return with the nominal X-ray clock, the late band returns 57.38-78.10 days later. Swift UVOT gives 47 late-phase UVW2 measurements in 2023 cycles 30 and 31, with 12 inside this band. They do not show the pulse expected for equal UV output per unit returning mass. With fixed published primary fluences, separate linear baselines and fitted independent Gaussian scatter, the late-to-primary UV yield ratio has a nominal one-sided 95 percent profile limit of 0.088. Imposed 3-, 7- and 14-day variability correlations weaken this limit to 0.182, 0.288 and 0.337. The result constrains a specified luminous completion of the delay model. It does not limit returned mass, reject other debris distributions, or establish an orbital stall. Spectral changes, response delays, uncertain primary fluences and more flexible baselines can weaken the inference. We supply code, input hashes, sensitivity results and a retrieval recipe; source observation tables stay outside the package.

display.caption: Observed late UV rates and the equal-yield pulse from the specified conserving debris model. The dashed curve uses the independent-noise profile limit. Correlated variability gives weaker limits.
